speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to narrow down the cause, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying these symptoms? Additionally, is the pain severe enough to prevent you from standing still, or does it move to your groin?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis).

Given the visible hematuria, right flank pain, and history of recurrent UTIs in a 42-year-old male, kidney stones are the most likely cause. To confirm this, I request a Urinalysis with microscopy and a Non-contrast CT KUB (Kidney, Ureter, Bladder).
